title: Oddness and balance of a homogeneous threshold
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and let $a_i\in\mathbb R$ be weights on the coordinates. Suppose that for every $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, $f(x)$ is the sign of $\sum_i a_i x_i$, with the convention that a nonnegative input gives $+1$, and that this sum is never zero on the cube. Then $f(-x)=-f(x)$ for every $x$, and the uniform mean of its real-valued sign representation is zero.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the sign cube to signs
At every cube point, $f$ is the threshold sign of the homogeneous linear form
The linear form is nonzero at every cube point
